title_prefix: Every notfound message re-runs a full sc
mechanism: The notfound handler (src/networking/protocol.lisp:855-882) declares no :rate-bucket, and check-peer-rate-limit allows any command whose handler declares none (src/networking/peer.lisp:1868-1876). It parses up to bl.ser:+max-inv-count+ = 50,000 entries with no size guard, and when any entry was a tx it calls process-tx-requests once per MESSAGE. process-tx-requests (:530-562) maphashes ALL of *tx-announcers* while holding the single global *tx-request-lock* that handle-inv also takes per announcement. Core's ReceivedNotFound (refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:288-294) is one indexed ReceivedResponse per item and nothing else; re-issues come from the per-peer GetRequestsToSend, whose GetRequestable walks only that peer's CANDIDATE_BEST announcements (refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:595-624); and the NOTFOUND branch discards the tx entries of any notfound carrying more than MAX_PEER_TX_ANNOUNCEMENTS + MAX_BLOCKS_IN_TRANSIT_PER_PEER = 5,016 invs (refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:5150-5164).
consequence: A 61-byte notfound buys a full scan of the tracker, and the pump admits +max-messages-per-peer-per-cycle+ = 32 messages per peer per pass, so about 2 KB of traffic from one peer converts into 31 ms of sync-thread CPU at the 5,000 tracked hashes a single attacker connection can reach on its own (MAX_PEER_TX_ANNOUNCEMENTS), and 319 ms at 50,000, all of it under the one lock the whole tx-relay path serialises on. The cost is unauthenticated, uncharged (no rate bucket, no misbehaviour score) and repeatable every pass. It is a DoS lever rather than a crash or unbounded growth -- the tracker itself is capped at 5,000 per peer -- so S2, not S1. The measurement matches the finder's within 5%. The oversized-notfound gap (50,000 accepted vs Core's 5,016) is the smaller half: the per-entry work is a hash lookup plus a short assoc, and one scan is charged per message regardless of the entry count, so the scheduler re-run is the lever, not the parse.
evidence: (1) ga11-p5-scan-cost, tracker filled from 1/5/10 peers at 5,000 announcements each: ((:PEERS 1 :TRACKED 5000 :MS-PER-SCAN-IN-FLIGHT 1.0 :MS-PER-SCAN-NO-CANDIDATE 1.0) (:PEERS 5 :TRACKED 25000 :MS-PER-SCAN-IN-FLIGHT 5.0 :MS-PER-SCAN-NO-CANDIDATE 5.0) (:PEERS 10 :TRACKED 50000 :MS-PER-SCAN-IN-FLIGHT 10.0 :MS-PER-SCAN-NO-CANDIDATE 10.1)) -- linear, and the same whether or not any candidate is selectable, so it is the scan and not the sending. (2) ga11-p5-notfound-cost, one 61-byte notfound through bl.net:handle-message at 50,000 tracked: (:TRACKED 50000 :PAYLOAD-BYTES 61 :MS-PER-NOTFOUND 9.95 :NOTFOUND-RATE-BUCKET NIL :MAX-INVS-ACCEPTED 50000 :MESSAGES-PER-PEER-PER-PASS 32). (3) ga11-p5-one-pass, 32 notfound messages (1,952 wire bytes) in one pump pass: 31.2 ms at 5,000 tracked and 319.4 ms at 50,000. (4) Positive control: the identical 32 messages against an EMPTY tracker cost 0.0 ms, so the whole cost is the tracker scan and not per-message overhead. Ours: src/networking/protocol.lisp:855-882, :530-562; src/networking/peer.lisp:1868-1876; src/networking/ibd.lisp:33 (+max-messages-per-peer-per-cycle+ 32); src/serialization/messages.lisp:464 (+max-inv-count+ 50000). Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:264-294; refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:5150-5164; refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:595-624.
fix_shape: Make the notfound response O(k) as Core's is. Drop the process-tx-requests call from the handler entirely and let the existing ~1 Hz scheduler pass re-route -- Core re-issues from SendMessages, not from the NOTFOUND branch -- or, if the prompt failover is worth keeping, replace the global scan with a targeted one that re-selects only the hashes named in this message, which is bounded by the message's own entry count. Add Core's size guard: ignore the tx entries of a notfound carrying more than +max-peer-tx-announcements+ + the per-peer blocks-in-transit cap (net_processing.cpp:5150-5164), and give the handler a :rate-bucket -- the serve bucket is the natural fit for an unsolicited response message -- so an uncharged command cannot exist on this path. Longer term the scan itself should not be global: Core keeps a per-peer index of CANDIDATE_BEST announcements so GetRequestsToSend touches only one peer's entries, and an index from peer to its candidate hashes here would make both the scheduler and the failover independent of the total tracked count.
